clue.text: Animal to have a meal tucking into fruit

indicators.note: tucking into says one piece is pushed inside the other, here the meal going into the fruit

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to have a meal is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone is told to eat some fruit, as if it were a dinner order.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla, chimp or orang-utan is a large primate, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Squall keeps doctor in a flutter

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the storm word wraps round the doctor

parts.note: a squall is a gale, a sudden strong wind
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A storm holds up a physician, leaving them flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flutter' reads as agitated, but 'flutter' is British slang for a small bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A flutter is British slang for a small bet, a wager on chance.

clue.text: Players have catalogue for recruit

parts.note: in bridge the players are named by compass points, here East and North
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A theatre company holds a list of people it might take on.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players sit at North, South, East and West, so two of them can stand for E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit someone, or to join up yourself, is to sign up for service.

clue.text: Art Hilton devised a sports event

indicators.note: devised means contrived or made up, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: Someone called Art Hilton has invented a new sporting competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A swim, cycle and run race is a multi-sport endurance competition.

clue.text: Smooth over hurtful published piece

parts.note: to smooth clothes is to press them
a cutting remark is hurtful

explanation.surface: An editor softens an unkind article before it goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipping from a newspaper is an article cut out after being printed.

clue.text: Complain persistently of Yankee's drive 'ome

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: 'ome is home with its H dropped, telling us to drop the H likewise

parts.note: to drive a nail is to hammer it

explanation.surface: An American grumbles about the drive back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ome, in the Cockney style, signals dropping the aitch from the word for drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is informal for whining or moaning on and on.

clue.text: Take responsibility for fuss over gymnastics

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: ado is fuss, as in much ado about nothing
PT is physical training, school gymnastics

explanation.surface: A coach takes charge of a row about the gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a child, a policy or a cause is to take it on as your own.

clue.text: Norma Jean almost got through African capital

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Norma Jean was the birth name of Marilyn Monroe
via means through, by way of

explanation.surface: A young woman nearly made it through to a city in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Liberia in West Africa.

clue.text: Rich senator upset about a bit of news

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the extra one
upset means knocked over, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
a bit of the word takes just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A wealthy politician is upset about a scrap of news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles SENATOR into RESOANT, and 'about' puts N from 'news' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich voice or sound is deep and full, ringing on.

clue.text: Prospector keeps sick retailer

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the prospector word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a prospector is a miner looking for ore
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A gold prospector looks after an unwell shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat-maker who sells hats is a kind of retailer.

clue.text: Money for drums

definitions.meaning: the British currency unit, in the plural
to drum is to beat repeatedly, as fists on a door

explanation.surface: Cash for a set of drums.
explanation.definitionFit: The sterling unit is money; and to beat hard and repeatedly is to drum.

clue.text: Parmesan's not unusual in Paris

definitions.note: a place found in Paris, an adjectival phrase standing for the district

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters take an unexpected order

parts.note: the cheese name with its s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Parmesan cheese is a common sight in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a district found in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: This Left Bank quarter, famous for its artists' cafés, lies in Paris.

clue.text: Composer's final letter found in inventory

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so the letter goes inside the inventory word

parts.note: an inventory is a list
Z is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A composer's last letter is discovered in a catalogue of effects.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz, the Hungarian Romantic pianist, was a famous composer.

clue.text: Film sad defeat

parts.note: to film a scene is to shoot it
down means sad, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A downbeat film about a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot down an argument or proposal is to defeat it soundly.

clue.text: Misconception about fallen woman going west is an example

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the misconception goes round the other piece

parts.note: an illusion is a misconception

indicators.note: going west in an across clue means reading right to left

parts.note: a tart is an old term for a fallen woman

explanation.surface: A mistaken belief about a disgraced woman heading west is offered as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fallen woman' is an old-fashioned euphemism; 'going west' is the reversal signal in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An illustration is a case cited to make a point clear, an instance.

clue.text: American cure meant heartless correction

parts.note: to end an ailment is to cure it

indicators.note: heartless means with the middle taken out, so the central letter goes

explanation.surface: An American remedy was supposed to be a ruthless fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A change made to a text or law to improve it is a correction.

clue.text: Clambers awkwardly in rough ascent

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone clambers clumsily up a rugged climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a climb over rough ground using hands as well as feet.

clue.text: Supporter is upset in the street? That's irritating!

indicators.note: in says these pieces sit inside the street word

parts.note: AVE is short for avenue, a street
a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked over in the street and finds it annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IS into SI; BRA and SI go 'in' AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrasive grates, harsh and annoying in manner.

clue.text: Major was once a skilled craftsman

definitions.text: Major was once a skilled craftsman

parts.words: Major was once a skilled craftsman
parts.note: John Major, as UK Prime Minister, formed a government team of ministers

explanation.surface: A former army major used to be a woodworker.
explanation.walkthrough: Major looks like a rank, but it is John Major, British Prime Minister 1990-97, who appointed his ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A furniture maker is a skilled woodworker, and a Prime Minister forms a government team.

clue.text: Stew gives soldier illness

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, so a gunner soldier
gout is a painful illness of the joints

explanation.surface: A dodgy stew makes a soldier ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned meat and vegetable stew.

clue.text: Museum student is a delinquent

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student at a museum turns out to be a young troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a person who wilfully damages property, a young offender.

clue.text: Intrepid maiden interrupts unknown Greek king

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: anon is short for anonymous, unknown
game means plucky, intrepid
M is a maiden over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A brave girl breaks in on an anonymous ancient ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Greeks at Troy as king of Mycenae.

clue.text: Dog beheaded bird

indicators.note: beheaded means its head is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

explanation.surface: A dog has decapitated a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Shot a scene

parts.note: a dram is a shot of spirits

explanation.surface: A film crew shoots a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a film term but is a small measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatre world is the stage scene, as in the London theatre scene.

clue.text: Union member embraces girl in game

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the bride wraps round the letter

parts.note: a bride is one member of a marriage union
G is an abbreviation for girl

explanation.surface: A trade unionist hugs a girl during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: This card game is played by four in two partnerships.

clue.text: A drug creates a a heavenly body

parts.note: a steroid is a drug, as used by cheating athletes

explanation.surface: Taking a drug turns someone into a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet orbiting the sun is a body in the heavens.

clue.text: The French rejected uniform for soccer team

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: le is French for the
even means uniform, level throughout

explanation.surface: The French turned down a kit for their football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer side fields eleven players.

clue.text: Supporter, on the whole, is temperate

parts.note: a tee supports the golf ball
the total is the whole amount

explanation.surface: A backer, by and large, is moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never drinks alcohol is temperate in the abstaining sense.
